A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same coupled signal-and-logit diffusion framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated content and the renamed audio appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification accuracies, speech-recognition WERs, ablations, and qualitative reconstruction results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluated baselines, standard-resolution ImageNet results, and an EARS computation-cost observation.

M1.justification: The Parallel, Alternating, and Nested algorithms, training objectives, frozen classifiers, and sampling schedules are retained. The deterministic clean-prediction explanation clarifies the existing procedure; suggested acceleration techniques are not implemented method changes.

E1.justification: Table 5 adds a standard-resolution ImageNet scenario at 224×224, extending image input conditions beyond the earlier downsampled ImageNet evaluation. Existing image and speech datasets and corruption types remain represented.

E2.justification: URIE is newly evaluated throughout the image comparisons in Table 1, and the Dissen enhancer throughout the speech comparisons in Table 2. Both works were already cited in v1, but these task-supervised enhancement comparators were absent from its reported comparisons. Their inclusion substantially expands comparison methods across both modalities.

E3.justification: The added ImageNet experiment uses a 10-class subset with a reported fixed sampling protocol and compares Parallel with Enhanced under the three existing corruptions. It supplements the retained 100-class, 32×32 experiment. Existing sampling budgets, classifier configurations, restricted-token speech decoding, and WER reference procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a limited scalability check asking whether coupling remains effective at standard image resolution, plus an empirical signal-versus-logit evaluation-cost comparison on EARS. The existing sampling-step, guidance-source, DDPM/DDIM, and qualitative reconstruction analyses are retained.

E5.justification: There are no additions to repeated-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing. New table entries continue point-estimate reporting. Appendix E's discussion of implicit uncertainty is conceptual rather than a statistical reporting change.

E6.justification: Existing scores are retained apart from equivalent rounding. Substantial new comparative results include URIE leading on MNIST, with 99.5% under blur versus 99.3% for the best coupled strategy, and Dissen WERs of 7.96%, 6.46%, and 13.04% in Table 2. Table 5 adds Enhanced/Parallel accuracies of 92.1/94.0, 86.5/92.4, and 94.0/94.1 for 15% noise, 30% noise, and blur. These are new comparisons, not improvements to previously reported same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–40, Propositions 3.1–3.2, and the appendix derivations are retained. Added explanations of posterior variance and deterministic clean prediction as a Dirac distribution clarify the existing point-estimate formulation without adding or revising mathematical results.

C1.justification: The main framework and three-strategy contributions remain unchanged. The conclusion extends the performance claim to enhancement methods using task supervision, explicitly naming URIE and Dissen, while qualifying superiority as holding in most settings.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 and new Appendix E expand runtime interpretations and strategy-selection guidance, including immediate feedback in Parallel and fixed-hypothesis limitations in Alternating. v2 also explains the MNIST exception and explicitly limits the high-resolution study to a 10-class proof of concept. These extend interpretation without establishing new causal validation.

D1.justification: v2 adds relative runtime information: one signal evaluation on EARS reportedly costs approximately seven logit evaluations. It also explicitly documents deterministic clean-sample prediction. Existing architecture, training, sampling, and code-access information is retained; implementation documentation for the new comparisons remains limited.

R1.justification: The new efficiency discussion adds references on faster solvers, distillation, DeepCache, flow formulations, and neural audio codecs. URIE and Dissen move from previously cited related approaches to explicit empirical comparisons. The foundational positioning against sequential enhancement, CARD, and joint energy-based models remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized notation and prose clarifications, adds a computational-complexity subsection and strategy-comparison appendix, and revises the conclusion. The audio appendix becomes Appendix F, and publication information and acknowledgements are updated. Most wording and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain comparator columns and revised captions, Table 5 is added, and Figure 4 gains horizontal baseline references and expanded legends while retaining the sampling curves. Other figures remain unchanged, with local float relocation and page reflow.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the evaluated task-supervised baselines in Tables 1–2 make the empirical comparison more informative, including the acknowledged MNIST exception. Table 5 provides a bounded resolution check, and notation and runtime explanations improve clarity. The gains remain limited because the new resolution study covers only ten classes, new experimental implementation details are sparse, and some added mechanism and runtime generalizations lack direct validation.
